title: Why a peacock's blue isn't pigment

scenes.headline: There's no blue pigment in a peacock feather.
The colour is built, not dyed.
scenes.body: Inside each barbule, tiny melanin rods held in keratin form a regular, crystal-like lattice.

scenes.headline: The rod spacing picks the colour.
scenes.body: Light bouncing off the lattice reinforces some wavelengths. Change the spacing, get a different colour.

scenes.headline: The proof: soak it, and the colour shifts.
scenes.body: Filling the lattice's air gaps with glycerin moved the reflected colour toward red. Pigment wouldn't do that.

scenes.headline: Every 'eye' on that train is physics, not paint.

caption:
A peacock's blue comes from structure, not blue pigment.

The same lattice of melanin rods makes every colour in the eyespot; blue, green, yellow and brown differ mainly in rod spacing and the number of layers.

Source: Zi J. et al. (2003) Coloration strategies in peacock feathers, PNAS 100:12576. Footage: Indian peafowl, Botanical Garden Hyderabad. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
